title: Frontiers | Impact of senolytic treatment on immunity, aging, and disease
abstract: Termed the SASP, these factors induce senescence in neighboring cells and consequently contribute to the aged tissue environment (Acosta et al., 2013). The senolytic capacity of fisetin was explored in a thorough 2018 study and included key insights into its effects on adaptive immune cells (Yousefzadeh et al., 2018). Progeroid mice fed chow supplemented with fisetin had a significant reduction in mRNA gene expression of *p16*, *p21*, and other SASP markers (e.g., IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β) in fat, spleen, liver, kidney, and peripheral CD3+ T cells measured at 20 weeks of age (Yousefzadeh et al., 2018). Short term treatment of fisetin (100 mg/kg for 5 consecutive days by oral gavage) resulted in a significant decrease in the proportion of flagged p16Ink4a expressing c-kit+ cells, CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, NK cells, and endothelial cells within adipose tissue when compared to aged untreated mice (Yousefzadeh et al., 2018).
